nodes.label: Caveman Response Style Convention
nodes.rationale: Terse agent prose keeps all technical substance while dropping articles, filler, hedging and pleasantries so responses cost fewer tokens; code, commits and PRs stay in normal prose, and the style is auto-dropped for security warnings, irreversible actions, or a confused user.

nodes.label: Tendril Network Hub Metaphor
nodes.rationale: The hero art depicts a single central figure grasping many bundles of threads that radiate outward to the edges of the frame, over a backdrop of branching lightning/tendril textures. This visually encodes the Tendril product idea: a central coordinator holding many outbound connections (nodes/leases/tunnels), i.e. one hub managing many distributed endpoints. The classical engraving style rendered in electric blue suggests old-world craft fused with electric/technical infrastructure.

nodes.label: Tendril
nodes.rationale: A pay-per-call compute marketplace for individuals rather than data centers — an agent-first take on Akash/io.net. Payment is the identity, so a brand-new address can pay on its first request with no sign-up and no sign-in.

nodes.label: x402 over USDC on Algorand
nodes.rationale: x402 is the only door: an unpaid request to any payable endpoint returns HTTP 402 naming an exact USDC amount. Chosen because the payment itself carries identity, removing accounts and sign-in from the money path entirely.

nodes.label: Ephemeral Docker sandbox (trust model)
nodes.rationale: The safety boundary is not a permissions system but a container: no host filesystem mounts, no inbound host ports, --cap-drop ALL plus no-new-privileges, cgroup CPU/memory/PID caps, destroyed the moment the paid lease ends. Accepted as the same containerization trade-off the whole DePIN compute sector runs on, just prepaid and individual-scale.

nodes.label: bore tunnel (outbound SSH exposure)
nodes.rationale: The sandbox dials out over bore instead of opening an inbound host port, so a contributor needs no port forwarding and no firewall change. bore is compiled from source in-image because upstream ships no arm64-linux binary; TUNNEL_MODE=local publishes SSH to 127.0.0.1 when consumer and agent share a machine.

nodes.label: Open-ended metered session
nodes.rationale: Renting buys no fixed block. A flat gate fee starts the clock; the session runs as long as credit covers the hourly rate and only the seconds actually used are billed at release. Chosen so nobody is disconnected at the end of a block they guessed wrong, and so a mid-session top-up simply moves the cut-off out.

nodes.label: Flat gate fee (FLAT_RENT_ATOMIC)
nodes.rationale: 0.01 USDC on-chain to open a session — a flat price needs no quote, no credit arithmetic and no session state, so the 402 flow stays a single round trip.

nodes.label: Settlement ordering: verify, work, settle
nodes.rationale: The facilitator verifies the atomic group by simulation, the backend provisions, and only then does the facilitator settle on chain — so a sandbox that fails to come up costs the caller nothing (503 with nothing settled).

nodes.label: Facilitator-sponsored network fee (USDC and zero ALGO)
nodes.rationale: The client signs only its own asset transfer; the facilitator signs and pays for the fee transaction. This removes ALGO from the client's requirements entirely, so an account can run to zero ALGO and still pay.
nodes.norm_label: facilitator-sponsored network fee (usdc and zero algo)

nodes.label: Payer identity from the settled transaction
nodes.rationale: Credit is keyed to the sender of the settled transaction, never to anything the client claims about itself — the only claim that cannot be forged without the key.
nodes.norm_label: payer identity from the settled transaction

nodes.label: Custodial off-chain credit ledger
nodes.rationale: Payments pool at one platform address and credit lives in Neon Postgres. Every payment is recorded by txid so a replay cannot credit twice. Contributor earnings are the part that does settle on-chain.

nodes.label: Credit watchdog
nodes.rationale: Checks every METER_INTERVAL_MS whether credit has run out, so worst-case overrun is one tick — absorbed by the platform, never billed past what the renter holds. The debit is clamped to the balance for exactly this reason.

nodes.label: Grace window (GRACE_ATOMIC)
nodes.rationale: Running dry must not cut a user off mid-keystroke, so the watchdog re-reads the live balance first and then opens GRACE_ATOMIC (default 1.00 USDC) of runtime at that lease's rate to save work in. Topping up clears it.

nodes.label: In-memory nodes and leases
nodes.rationale: Only money state hits Postgres. Heartbeats and the watchdog never write to the DB, which keeps it quiet; the accepted cost is that a registry restart drops live sessions — acceptable because the sockets die anyway.

nodes.label: One Postgres schema per network
nodes.rationale: Tables live in testnet.* or mainnet.* and search_path points at the right one, so testnet play money can never be read as a mainnet balance. An unrecognised ALGORAND_NETWORK throws at boot because silently running testnet while believing you configured mainnet is worse than not starting. Side effect: public holds no tables, so unqualified SQL fails.

nodes.label: Bazaar discovery metadata
nodes.rationale: Settling and being discoverable are separate systems: a settlement proves an address paid an amount but carries no method, input shape or example output, so there is nothing to build a catalog entry from. Tendril declares the metadata in every 402 instead, declared once in backend/src/x402/discovery.ts. PUBLIC_BASE_URL is the trap — unset behind a proxy catalogs you as localhost:4000.

nodes.label: CORS-free payable routes
nodes.rationale: Payable routes answer any origin so any browser can pay one; the 402 is what protects them and the price is the same whoever asks. The Tendril web app therefore has no privileged access — it is just another x402 client. CORS_ORIGIN still guards everything else, and CORS only ever constrained browsers anyway.

nodes.label: On-chain contributor payout
nodes.rationale: The contributor is paid in USDC out of what was actually collected, minus PLATFORM_FEE_PCT — never out of what was merely owed. If PLATFORM_PRIVATE_KEY is unset or the payout address never opted into the ASA, the payout is recorded unpaid and the node flagged payoutBlocked.

nodes.label: SSH auth: pubkey or wallet-address password
nodes.rationale: sshPubKey becomes the container's authorized_keys and is the only option that works without a session, since there is no wallet address to use as a password. The fallback per-lease password is the wallet address — fine for ephemeral throwaway root compute, but it is a password, not a key.
nodes.norm_label: ssh auth: pubkey or wallet-address password

nodes.label: Session token exists only to read a balance
nodes.rationale: Paying needs no account at all, so sign-in shrank to proving ownership of an address in order to spend existing credit. Unauthenticated callers can hint ?payer= but the discount is floored at MIN_PAYABLE_ATOMIC so nobody can drain a stranger's balance.
nodes.norm_label: session token exists only to read a balance

nodes.label: Vite SPA over Next.js for web/
nodes.rationale: The wallet stack is client-only, so an SPA avoids SSR/hydration friction. Consequence: the web app is not dockerized, it is a static build dropped on any host.
nodes.norm_label: vite spa over next.js for web/

nodes.label: npm-workspaces monorepo layout
nodes.rationale: backend/, contributor/, web/, example-buyer/ are self-contained pieces; shared/ holds types, the WebSocket contract and pricing helpers imported by all as @tendril/shared.

nodes.label: Contributor agent daemon
nodes.rationale: Proves node ownership by signing a nonce, heartbeats over WebSocket, and mounts the host Docker socket to launch each rented sandbox as a sibling container — so there is no Docker-in-Docker and nothing extra to install.

nodes.label: example-buyer autonomous training agent
nodes.rationale: Headless proof that the payment is the identity: tops up over x402, discovers, rents, runs a script, releases — zero clicks and no sign-in.

nodes.label: GET /platform
nodes.rationale: Call it first — a client should take network and asset from here rather than hard-coding them, because they follow the server's ALGORAND_NETWORK.

nodes.label: GET /explorer
nodes.rationale: Free on purpose so an agent can survey the market before spending anything. Only online, heartbeating nodes appear; an empty list is normal, not an error.

nodes.label: GET /metrics
nodes.rationale: Public aggregates derived entirely from top-ups and charges, with no PII beyond addresses already public on-chain. Units differ per leaderboard: atomic USDC, seconds, or lease counts.

nodes.label: POST /auth/wallet-login
nodes.rationale: The signature is over a 0-ALGO self-payment whose note is the nonce — verified and discarded, never broadcast, so signing in costs nothing and needs no balance. Returns a 7-day JWT to be treated as a bearer secret.

nodes.label: GET /wallet
nodes.rationale: The one thing a session is for. A headless client typically has no session and cannot call it; credit surfaces to it instead via billing.creditAtomic on a successful rent and the 402 insufficient_credit body.

nodes.label: GET /lease/:id (status)
nodes.rationale: expiresAt is when credit runs out at the current rate and moves when you top up; graceUntil turning non-null is the only warning before the sandbox is destroyed, so poll this if you care about not losing work.

nodes.label: DELETE /x402/leases/:id (release)
nodes.rationale: Free and safe to call twice. This is when compute is billed — nothing was taken when the session opened. Alias: POST /lease/:id/release.

nodes.label: Three independent credentials (session, lease, payment)
nodes.rationale: None of the three is required to pay, because payment identifies itself. A session grants reading your own balance; a lease token grants status/run/release for one lease; a payment grants the paid action, with the payer being the transaction's sender.

nodes.label: Plain HTTP error index
nodes.rationale: Every error is {"error": "<code>"}, some with detail or extra fields such as minimum, maximum or txid.

nodes.label: Atomic-unit amount convention
nodes.rationale: All amounts are integer atomic units of USDC (6 decimals) — strings where they cross the wire in x402 payloads, numbers in the plain endpoints, because a JSON number cannot carry a uint64 safely.

nodes.label: POST /topup
nodes.rationale: No auth, CORS open, price is whatever you ask for between MIN_TOPUP_ATOMIC and MAX_TOPUP_ATOMIC. Credit is keyed to the settled transaction's sender, so paying from an address you cannot sign for (an exchange withdrawal) creates a balance nobody can spend. Replays return 200 with the original receipt and credit nothing further — idempotent because a top-up buys nothing consumable.

nodes.label: POST /rent/:nodeId
nodes.rationale: One flat on-chain gate fee is the only thing that moves up front; the seconds used are billed from credit once, at close. The credit check runs after verify() and before settle(), so an address that cannot fund MIN_LEASE_SECONDS is turned away without paying the gate fee rather than charged for a session the watchdog would kill on its next tick.

nodes.label: POST /lease/:id/run
nodes.rationale: The job runs before the payment settles, so a job that never ran is never paid for. A failed job (ok:false) is still a 200 and still charged — the compute was consumed. Exists only for clients that want one-shot execution without holding a shell.

nodes.label: DELETE /x402/leases/:id
nodes.rationale: Free, because closing should never be something a user avoids. Idempotent via a unique charges.lease_id, so a concurrent release and watchdog tick cannot bill the same session twice — the loser returns zeros and the current balance.

nodes.label: Billing formula (usedAtomic, charged, payout)
nodes.rationale: usedAtomic = ceil(usedSeconds/3600 x rate); charged = min(usedAtomic, balance); payout = charged x (1 - PLATFORM_FEE_PCT/100). charged is clamped to the balance because the watchdog only ticks every METER_INTERVAL_MS, so a session can legitimately overrun by one tick — the platform absorbs it and the contributor is paid out of what was collected, never out of what was merely owed.

nodes.label: PaymentRequired schema
nodes.rationale: accepts always has exactly one entry because Tendril takes one asset on one network. The same object is served both as the 402 body and as base64 in the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header, so a client can read whichever is convenient.

nodes.label: PaymentRequirements schema
nodes.rationale: extra.feePayer present means build the two-transaction group and sign only index 0; absent means build a one-transaction group and pay your own fee, which requires ALGO.

nodes.label: PaymentPayload schema
nodes.rationale: paymentGroup must already carry a valid group id; paymentIndex names your signed transfer, the other entry is the fee payer's and is left unsigned.

nodes.label: SandboxAccess schema
nodes.rationale: Carries a ready-to-paste ssh command plus authMethod publickey or password, so the caller never has to assemble host/port/user itself.

nodes.label: Error envelope and the two shapes of 402
nodes.rationale: A 402 meaning 'pay this' has a PaymentRequired body; a 402 meaning 'your payment cannot proceed' (settlement_failed, insufficient_credit) has an error envelope. Clients must branch on the presence of accepts, not on the status code alone.
nodes.norm_label: error envelope and the two shapes of 402

nodes.label: Three-round-trip payment flow
nodes.rationale: verify() only simulates — nothing reaches the chain — the server does the work in that gap and settles afterwards. The middle round trip is where the money would be lost if the ordering were wrong.

nodes.label: x402 request/response headers
nodes.rationale: PAYMENT-SIGNATURE is a non-simple header so every paid browser request is preflighted; the three response headers must be in Access-Control-Expose-Headers or a paid response would look unpaid to JavaScript. X-PAYMENT and X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE are kept as legacy aliases.

nodes.label: Single-use payment signature
nodes.rationale: Replaying a signed header returns the original receipt on /topup (idempotent) but 409 payment_already_used on /rent and /run, because those buy something consumable.

nodes.label: First-run failure: asset not opted in
nodes.rationale: A correctly built payment that cannot be simulated returns a fresh 402 carrying the facilitator's own message. The common case is the paying address never opting into the ASA; the sibling case names PLATFORM_PAYTO and is an operator problem, not a client one. Simulation catches it before anything is submitted, so nothing settles and nothing is charged.
nodes.norm_label: first-run failure: asset not opted in

nodes.label: What is safe to retry
nodes.rationale: Every failure mode except 409 payment_already_used moved no money and is safe to retry; that one alone requires building a new payment.

nodes.label: Server configuration variables
nodes.rationale: X402_NETWORK must match the facilitator's /supported byte for byte and is checked loudly at boot, because a mismatch fails every payment at verify time.

nodes.label: Renting from the CLI
nodes.rationale: curl can do everything except the three paid calls, because paying means building and signing an Algorand atomic group — there is no hand-writable header that stands in for a signature. Roughly 20 lines of JavaScript covers the rest.

nodes.label: Signer interface (signTransactions with indexes)
nodes.rationale: Signing only the requested indexes and returning null for the rest is what leaves the fee-payer transaction unsigned for the facilitator. @txnlab/use-wallet's signTransactions already matches this shape, so browser and headless clients share one code path and differ only in the signer.

nodes.label: Losing leaseToken means you cannot release
nodes.rationale: The token is returned once and stored nowhere readable back; lose it and the session runs until credit is exhausted. Combined with 'always release', this is the main operational hazard of the metered model.
nodes.norm_label: losing leasetoken means you cannot release
